name: Can a walk-in shower be installed without removing the rest of the bathroom floor?

mainEntity.name: Is it possible to install a walk-in shower while leaving the rest of the bathroom floor in place?
mainEntity.text: Is it possible to install a walk-in shower while leaving the rest of the bathroom floor in place?

acceptedAnswer.text: It may be possible to keep part of the existing bathroom floor, but only if the new shower can tie into it without creating height problems or waterproofing weaknesses. Walk-in showers often need floor reconstruction near the shower footprint so the drain slope, waterproofing membrane, and threshold transition all work correctly. If the new shower is curbless or low-threshold, the surrounding floor height becomes even more important. Keeping the rest of the bathroom floor in place can save time and money, but it is not worth it if the result creates awkward transitions, poor drainage, or leak risk. The floor should be evaluated as one system, not as separate finish layers. In many remodels, a partial rebuild around the shower area is the cleanest way to protect the long-term performance of the bathroom while minimizing unnecessary demolition.
acceptedAnswer.description: Sometimes, but only if the new shower height, drain slope, and waterproofing can integrate cleanly with the existing floor. In many remodels, some surrounding flooring must be removed or rebuilt to create the right transition and protect against leaks. The answer depends on structure, elevation, and the shower design.
